```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Run from the project root regardless of RStudio's knit-directory setting.
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r calculate, include=FALSE}
source("setup.R")

water_supplies <- get_wsd(rapid = TRUE)
all_conus <- get_wsd(conus = TRUE, fill_empty_coords = TRUE)

importance <- calc_system_importance(water_supplies,
                                     all_water_supplies = all_conus,
                                     return_details = TRUE)

results <- importance$results
results_all <- importance$all_sources
sdwa_inactive <- importance$sdwa_inactive
rapid_source_ids <- unique(water_supplies$wsd_source_id)

# Settings used by the function, for the text and rule tables below
list2env(importance$settings, envir = environment())

# Results with source locations, for maps
system_importance <- water_supplies |>
  distinct(wsd_source_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(wsd_source_id) |>
  inner_join(results, by = "wsd_source_id")

# All CONUS sources before inactive ones are removed, used only for the counts in Step 1
all_conus_sources <- all_conus |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  distinct(wsd_source_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

park_run_categories <- c("Non-PWS", "Low", "Moderate", "High")
pws_categories <- c("Low", "Moderate", "High")

busy_parks <- results |>
  filter(park_visitation_class == "High") |>
  pull(park_unit) |>
  unique()

show_table <- function(data, height = NULL, ...) {
  table <- data |>
    kable(digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), ...) |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
  if (is.null(height)) table else scroll_box(table, height = height)
}

fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)

category_colors <- c("High" = "#8C2B0E", "Moderate" = "#CB7223", "Low" = "#DFCB34",
                     "Non-PWS" = "#7FA4C2", "Municipal/purchased" = "#68434E",
                     "Non-potable" = "#289A84", "Proposed" = "grey60")

importance_colors <- c("High" = "#8C2B0E", "Moderate" = "#CB7223", "Low" = "#DFCB34",
                       "Not rated" = "grey60")

role_colors <- c("Primary" = "#8C2B0E", "Secondary" = "#CB7223", "Minor" = "#DFCB34",
                 "Staff only" = "#7FA4C2", "Not park-run" = "grey60")

# Map a column with fixed colors, dropping values that aren't present
factor_map <- function(data, column, colors, label) {
  data[[column]] <- droplevels(factor(as.character(data[[column]]), levels = names(colors)))
  mapview(data, zcol = column, layer.name = label, map.types = NULL,
          col.regions = unname(colors[levels(data[[column]])])) |>
    add_nps_basemaps()
}
```

## Purpose

This value shows how important each water system is to its park. It isn't scored as a
rapid indicator, so it isn't normalized. Each source gets one **importance category**
(High, Moderate, Low, or Not rated) with a reason, used to filter or add context to the
rapid results.

A park's visitors can't be divided among its water systems reliably. Many visitors use no
park water, some parks buy most of their water, and SDWA doesn't report a park's share of
a municipal utility. So the method rates each system on two separate things, then
combines them with park visitation:

- **Scale:** how many people the system serves, compared with systems everywhere.
- **Park role:** how central the system is to its own park.

Steps 1 to 7 below explain each piece of the logic in order.

## Final importance by source

```{r final-counts}
results |>
  group_by(`Importance category` = importance_category) |>
  summarize(Sources = n(), Parks = n_distinct(park_unit),
            `Busy parks` = n_distinct(park_unit[park_visitation_class == "High"])) |>
  show_table()
```

```{r final-map}
factor_map(system_importance, "importance_category", importance_colors, "Importance category")
```

Every source on the rapid list, sorted by category and then park. Steps 2 to 6 explain
the scale, role, and visitation columns.

```{r final-table}
results |>
  arrange(importance_category, park_unit, water_system_name, wsd_source_id) |>
  transmute(`Source ID` = wsd_source_id,
            Park = park_unit,
            System = water_system_name,
            `Importance category` = importance_category,
            Reason = importance_reason,
            Scale = system_category,
            Population = population_estimate,
            `Park role` = park_role,
            `Park visitation` = park_visitation_class) |>
  show_table(height = "600px")
```

## Step 1: Import sources and remove inactive ones

All CONUS sources come from `get_wsd(conus = TRUE, fill_empty_coords = TRUE)`, including
municipal, purchased, and hauled supplies. Inactive sources are removed before anything
else is calculated:

- Inactive or temporarily inactive in the WSD. A missing status counts as active.
- The source's PWS isn't active in SDWA. These are listed under
  [Data clarification needed](#data-clarification-needed).

```{r step1-counts}
wsd_inactive <- all_conus_sources |> filter(coalesce(active, "active") != "active")

tibble(
  Step = c("All CONUS sources",
           "Removed: inactive or temporarily inactive in the WSD",
           "Removed: PWS not active in SDWA",
           "Kept: active sources"),
  Sources = c(nrow(all_conus_sources), nrow(wsd_inactive), nrow(sdwa_inactive), nrow(results_all)),
  Parks = c(n_distinct(all_conus_sources$park_unit), n_distinct(wsd_inactive$park_unit),
            n_distinct(sdwa_inactive$park_unit), n_distinct(results_all$park_unit)),
  `On rapid list` = c(sum(all_conus_sources$wsd_source_id %in% rapid_source_ids),
                      sum(wsd_inactive$wsd_source_id %in% rapid_source_ids),
                      sum(sdwa_inactive$wsd_source_id %in% rapid_source_ids),
                      sum(results_all$wsd_source_id %in% rapid_source_ids))
) |>
  show_table()
```

## Step 2: Rate scale from population served

Population served is `POPULATION_SERVED_COUNT` from the SDWA public water system table,
matched on PWS number. Sources with two PWS numbers use the active record, then the
larger population. The first matching row sets each source's category:

```{r step2-rules}
tribble(
  ~Order, ~Category, ~Rule, ~`Population used`,
  1, "Proposed", "Classification is Proposed System", "None",
  2, "Non-potable", "Classification is Non-Potable (NonPOT)", "None",
  3, "Municipal/purchased", "Municipal, purchased, hauled, or tribal source that isn't federally owned", "None",
  4, "Non-PWS", "Classification is Non-Public Water System, with no SDWA population", paste0(assumed_pop_non_pws, " (assumed)"),
  5, "Low", paste0("Population served of ", tier_low_max, " or less"), paste0("SDWA, or ", assumed_pop_pws, " (assumed) if the PWS number has no usable match"),
  6, "Moderate", paste0("Population served of ", tier_low_max + 1, " to ", fmt(tier_moderate_max)), "SDWA",
  7, "High", paste0("Population served above ", fmt(tier_moderate_max)), "SDWA"
) |>
  show_table()
```

The `r tier_low_max` and `r fmt(tier_moderate_max)` breaks follow EPA's "very small" and
"small" system size classes. Municipal supplies get no population because SDWA reports
the whole utility, as these examples show:

```{r step2-municipal}
results_all |>
  filter(system_category == "Municipal/purchased", !is.na(population_served)) |>
  distinct(pws_name, population_served, park_unit) |>
  group_by(`SDWA system` = pws_name, `SDWA population` = population_served) |>
  summarize(Parks = paste(sort(unique(park_unit)), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(`SDWA population`)) |>
  head(5) |>
  show_table(caption = "Largest populations among municipal supplies")
```

```{r step2-counts}
results |>
  group_by(Category = system_category) |>
  summarize(Sources = n(), Parks = n_distinct(park_unit)) |>
  show_table(caption = "Rapid sources by category")
```

```{r step2-map}
factor_map(system_importance, "system_category", category_colors, "Scale category")
```

## Step 3: Separate staff-only systems

`point_of_use` is free text, so it's grouped by keyword. The first matching group wins,
so a system serving a visitor center and staff housing counts as visitor-facing. Only the
Staff/admin group changes the result: those systems are left out of the park role
comparison in Step 4. "Other" and "Missing" count as visitor-facing.

```{r step3-patterns}
tibble(Group = names(pou_patterns),
       Keywords = pou_patterns |> str_remove_all(fixed("\\b")) |> str_replace_all(fixed("|"), ", ")) |>
  show_table()
```

```{r step3-counts}
results |>
  filter(system_category %in% park_run_categories) |>
  count(Group = pou_type, Category = system_category) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Category, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  show_table(caption = "Park-run rapid sources by point-of-use group and category")
```

## Step 4: Assign a park role

Each park's own potable systems (Non-PWS, Low, Moderate, High) are compared with each
other. Each PWS counts once, however many sources it has. Roles use all active sources,
not only those on the rapid list.

- **Primary:** the park's largest visitor-facing system. Systems with the same
  population are all primary.
- **Secondary:** any other visitor-facing system serving at least
  `r 100 * secondary_share_min`% of the park's visitor-facing population.
- **Minor:** any other visitor-facing system.
- **Staff only:** every source of the system is in the Staff/admin group.
- **Not park-run:** municipal, non-potable, and proposed sources.

```{r step4-counts}
results |>
  count(Role = park_role, Scale = system_category) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Scale, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  show_table(caption = "Rapid sources by park role and scale")
```

```{r step4-map}
factor_map(system_importance, "park_role", role_colors, "Park role")
```

## Step 5: Add park context

- **Busy park:** mean annual recreation visits (`TRV`), 2020--2024, of at least
  `r fmt(park_vis_high)`. Total visits (`TV`) aren't used because they include
  non-recreation traffic such as commuters.
- **Municipal check:** the park has fewer municipal connections than park-run systems.
  Parks that fail may get most of their water from a utility, so their own largest system
  isn't treated as their main supply. The connection count doesn't reflect how much water
  each one supplies.

```{r step5-counts}
results |>
  group_by(park_unit) |>
  summarize(class = first(park_visitation_class),
            passes = first(n_municipal) < first(n_park_run)) |>
  group_by(`Visitation class` = factor(class, levels = c("High", "Moderate", "Low", "No data"))) |>
  summarize(Parks = n(), `Pass municipal check` = sum(passes), `Fail municipal check` = sum(!passes)) |>
  show_table(caption = "Rapid parks by visitation class and municipal check")
```

## Step 6: Assign the importance category

The first matching row sets each source's category. Every row that uses the park role
only applies to a PWS (Low, Moderate, or High scale) at a park that passes the municipal
check. Non-PWS systems can't qualify through the park role, because they serve fewer than
25 people per day by definition.

```{r step6-rules}
tribble(
  ~Order, ~Category, ~Reason, ~Rule,
  1, "Not rated", "Non-potable, Municipal or purchased, or Proposed", "Scale category is one of these",
  2, "High", "High scale", paste0("Serves more than ", fmt(tier_moderate_max), " people"),
  3, "High", "Primary system at a busy park", paste0("Primary role at a park with ", fmt(park_vis_high), "+ recreation visits"),
  4, "Moderate", "Moderate scale", paste0("Serves ", tier_low_max + 1, " to ", fmt(tier_moderate_max), " people"),
  5, "Moderate", "Primary system at a moderately busy park", paste0("Primary role at a park with ", fmt(park_vis_moderate), " to ", fmt(park_vis_high), " recreation visits"),
  6, "Moderate", "Secondary system at a busy park", paste0("Secondary role at a park with ", fmt(park_vis_high), "+ recreation visits"),
  7, "Low", "Staff-only system", "Park role is Staff only",
  8, "Low", "Non-public system", "Scale is Non-PWS",
  9, "Low", "Small system", "Everything else: a Low-scale PWS without a qualifying role"
) |>
  show_table()
```

```{r step6-counts}
results |>
  count(`Importance category` = importance_category, Reason = importance_reason, name = "Sources") |>
  left_join(results |>
              group_by(Reason = importance_reason) |>
              summarize(Parks = n_distinct(park_unit)),
            by = "Reason") |>
  show_table(caption = "Rapid sources by importance category and reason")
```

## Step 7: Filter to the rapid list

The table is limited to sources returned by `get_wsd(rapid = TRUE)`. Roles and municipal
counts were calculated before this filter, so they still reflect each park's full set of
systems.

```{r step7-counts}
tibble(
  Step = c("Active sources", "Active sources on the rapid list"),
  Sources = c(nrow(results_all), nrow(results)),
  Parks = c(n_distinct(results_all$park_unit), n_distinct(results$park_unit)),
  High = c(sum(results_all$importance_category == "High"), sum(results$importance_category == "High")),
  Moderate = c(sum(results_all$importance_category == "Moderate"), sum(results$importance_category == "Moderate"))
) |>
  show_table()
```

## Parks with no High system

Most parks have no High system. That's expected: outside busy parks, a system needs a
High scale to qualify.

```{r not-captured-overview}
results |>
  group_by(park_unit) |>
  summarize(class = first(park_visitation_class), any_high = any(high_importance)) |>
  group_by(`Visitation class` = factor(class, levels = c("High", "Moderate", "Low", "No data"))) |>
  summarize(Parks = n(), `With a High source` = sum(any_high),
            Without = sum(!any_high)) |>
  show_table()
```

### Busy parks with no High system

```{r busy-missed}
# Judged on all active sources, because a park's primary system may not be on the rapid list
busy_missed <- results_all |>
  filter(park_unit %in% busy_parks,
         !park_unit %in% results$park_unit[results$high_importance]) |>
  group_by(park_unit) |>
  summarize(
    `Recreation visits` = round(first(park_rec_visits)),
    `Park-run systems` = first(n_park_run),
    `Municipal connections` = first(n_municipal),
    `Primary system` = paste(unique(water_system_name[park_role == "Primary"]), collapse = "; "),
    `Primary population` = if (any(park_role == "Primary")) max(population_estimate[park_role == "Primary"]) else NA_real_,
    primary_is_pws = any(park_role == "Primary" & system_category %in% pws_categories),
    primary_on_rapid = any(park_role == "Primary" & wsd_source_id %in% rapid_source_ids),
    passes_municipal = first(n_municipal) < first(n_park_run)
  ) |>
  mutate(Reason = case_when(
    `Park-run systems` == 0 ~ "No park-run systems: all water is municipal, purchased, or hauled",
    !primary_is_pws ~ "Primary system isn't a PWS",
    !passes_municipal ~ "Fails the municipal check",
    !primary_on_rapid ~ "Primary system isn't on the rapid list",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  ),
  `Passes municipal check` = passes_municipal) |>
  select(-primary_is_pws, -primary_on_rapid, -passes_municipal) |>
  rename(Park = park_unit) |>
  arrange(Reason, desc(`Recreation visits`))

show_table(busy_missed)
```

```{r busy-missed-map}
factor_map(filter(system_importance, park_unit %in% busy_missed$Park), "system_category",
           category_colors, "Busy parks with no High system")
```

## Data clarification needed

Each item below is a place where the databases may be wrong or incomplete, with a
suggested way to confirm it. Within each table, sources that are currently High come
first, because a correction there is most likely to change a result.

```{r clarification-summary}
busy_municipal_fail <- busy_missed |>
  filter(Reason == "Fails the municipal check") |>
  pull(Park)

tribble(
  ~`#`, ~Item, ~Sources, ~`Currently High`, ~`How to confirm`,
  1, "Population far above visits",
  sum(results$review_population_vs_visits), sum(results$high_importance & results$review_population_vs_visits),
  "Check the PWS in the state drinking water viewer or SDWIS, and the latest OPH sanitary survey",
  2, "SDWA population may not describe the park",
  sum(results$review_population), sum(results$high_importance & results$review_population),
  "Confirm who owns and uses the PWS; reclassify as municipal in the WSD if it's a utility",
  3, "PWS with an assumed population",
  sum(results$review_assumed_pws), sum(results$high_importance & results$review_assumed_pws),
  "Fix the PWS number in the WSD, or look it up in SDWA by system name",
  4, "Tied primary systems",
  sum(results$review_tied_primary), sum(results$high_importance & results$review_tied_primary),
  "Break the tie with OPH survey populations or water use records",
  5, "PWS sorted as staff only",
  sum(results$review_staff_only_pws), sum(results$high_importance & results$review_staff_only_pws),
  "Read the WSD description; add a keyword or a manual correction",
  6, "Busy parks failing the municipal check",
  sum(results$park_unit %in% busy_municipal_fail & results$system_category %in% pws_categories), 0L,
  "Compare purchased and produced water volumes in park water use records",
  7, "Classification and use category disagree",
  sum(results$review_potable_conflict), sum(results$high_importance & results$review_potable_conflict),
  "Check the OPH survey or ask the park; correct one field in the WSD",
  8, "Active in the WSD but not in SDWA",
  nrow(sdwa_inactive), 0L,
  "Check SDWA for a deactivation date or a replacement PWS number"
) |>
  show_table()
```

### 1. Population far above recreation visits

SDWA population is at or above average recreation visits per day. Busy seasons, staff,
and residents can explain some of these, but others may be errors, such as Martin Van
Buren's 10,000.

**How to confirm:**

- Check that the PWS number matches the system: compare `SDWA system` with `System`.
- Look up the PWS in the state drinking water viewer or SDWIS. Check the population type
  (residential, transient, non-transient) and whether the count has changed over time.
- Compare with the population in the park's latest OPH sanitary survey.
- If SDWA is wrong, record the corrected population so it can override SDWA.

```{r clarify-population-visits}
results |>
  filter(review_population_vs_visits) |>
  distinct(park_unit, unit_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(ratio = population_estimate / (park_rec_visits / 365)) |>
  arrange(desc(high_importance), desc(ratio)) |>
  transmute(Park = park_unit,
            System = water_system_name,
            `SDWA system` = pws_name,
            `PWS number` = pws_number_clean,
            `SDWA type` = pws_type_desc,
            Population = population_estimate,
            `Recreation visits` = round(park_rec_visits),
            `Times visits per day` = ratio,
            `Importance category` = importance_category) |>
  show_table(height = "400px")
```

### 2. SDWA population may not describe the park

These are federally owned systems with a municipal, purchased, hauled, or tribal source,
and non-federal community water systems listed as park-run. Their SDWA population may
include people outside the park, such as a military base or a town.

**How to confirm:**

- Check the PWS owner and service area in SDWA or the state viewer.
- Ask the park whether the system also serves non-NPS users.
- If it's a utility the park buys from, change `source_type` in the WSD to municipal or
  purchased. It then moves to the Municipal/purchased category.

```{r clarify-population-park}
results |>
  filter(review_population) |>
  arrange(desc(high_importance), desc(population_estimate)) |>
  transmute(Park = park_unit,
            System = water_system_name,
            `SDWA system` = pws_name,
            Owner = owner_type_desc,
            `SDWA type` = pws_type_desc,
            `Source type` = source_type,
            Population = population_estimate,
            `Importance category` = importance_category) |>
  show_table(height = "350px")
```

### 3. PWS with an assumed population

These sources are classified as public water systems, but their PWS number didn't match
an SDWA record with a population, so they're given `r assumed_pop_pws` people. The real
population could move them into a different scale or change which system is primary.

**How to confirm:**

- Check the PWS number format in the WSD, such as a missing state prefix or extra
  characters.
- Search SDWA by system name and state to find the right PWS number.
- Update `pws_number` in the WSD.

```{r clarify-assumed}
results |>
  filter(review_assumed_pws) |>
  arrange(desc(high_importance), desc(park_rec_visits)) |>
  transmute(Park = park_unit,
            System = water_system_name,
            Classification = classification,
            `PWS number in WSD` = pws_number_clean,
            Role = park_role,
            `Recreation visits` = round(park_rec_visits),
            `Importance category` = importance_category) |>
  show_table(height = "350px")
```

### 4. Tied primary systems

When several systems at a park have the same population, they're all primary. Ties
usually mean the populations are defaults or rough estimates, so the real main system
can't be told apart.

**How to confirm:**

- Compare populations in the park's OPH sanitary survey.
- Compare annual water use for each system, for example in
  `data/Water_Supply_Systems/Manual_Water_Use_from_IRMA.xlsx`.
- If one system is clearly larger, correct its population.

```{r clarify-ties}
results |>
  filter(review_tied_primary) |>
  distinct(park_unit, water_system_name, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(desc(high_importance), park_unit) |>
  transmute(Park = park_unit,
            System = water_system_name,
            `Point of use` = point_of_use,
            Population = population_estimate,
            Source = population_source,
            Scale = system_category,
            `Tied systems` = n_tied_primary,
            `Importance category` = importance_category) |>
  show_table(height = "400px")
```

### 5. PWS sorted as staff only

These public water systems were left out of the park role comparison because their
`point_of_use` matched only staff keywords. If visitors use them, the park's primary
system could change.

**How to confirm:**

- Read the `point_of_use` text below and the WSD `description` field.
- If a system serves visitors, add the missing keyword to the Lodging, Campground, or
  Visitor day use group, or record a manual correction for that system.

```{r clarify-staff-only}
results |>
  filter(review_staff_only_pws) |>
  distinct(park_unit, water_system_name, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(desc(park_rec_visits)) |>
  transmute(Park = park_unit,
            System = water_system_name,
            `Point of use` = point_of_use,
            Population = population_estimate,
            Scale = system_category,
            `Busy park` = park_visitation_class == "High") |>
  show_table(height = "400px")
```

### 6. Busy parks failing the municipal check

These busy parks have at least as many municipal connections as park-run systems, so
their largest system isn't counted. The check counts connections, not volume, so a park
may still get most of its water from its own system.

**How to confirm:**

- Compare the volume each park buys with the volume it produces, from park water use or
  utility billing records (for example `Manual_Water_Use_from_IRMA.xlsx`).
- Ask the park whether the municipal connections serve major visitor areas.
- If the park's own system supplies most of the water, it should pass the check.

```{r clarify-municipal}
results_all |>
  filter(park_unit %in% busy_municipal_fail,
         system_category %in% c(pws_categories, "Municipal/purchased")) |>
  distinct(park_unit, water_system_name, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(park_unit, system_category) |>
  transmute(Park = park_unit,
            System = water_system_name,
            Category = system_category,
            Role = park_role,
            Population = population_estimate,
            `Source type` = source_type,
            `Point of use` = point_of_use) |>
  show_table(height = "400px")
```

### 7. Classification and use category disagree

Classification sets the Non-potable category. These sources have a `use_category` that
suggests otherwise, so they may be in the wrong category.

**How to confirm:**

- Check the latest OPH sanitary survey or ask the park whether the source supplies
  drinking water.
- Correct `classification` or `use_category` in the WSD.

```{r clarify-potable}
results |>
  filter(review_potable_conflict) |>
  arrange(desc(high_importance), park_unit) |>
  transmute(Park = park_unit,
            System = water_system_name,
            Classification = classification,
            `Use category` = use_category,
            Category = system_category,
            `Importance category` = importance_category) |>
  show_table(height = "350px")
```

### 8. Active in the WSD but not in SDWA

These sources were removed in Step 1 because their PWS isn't active in SDWA, but the WSD
lists them as active. Some may still be in use under a new PWS number.

**How to confirm:**

- Look up the PWS in SDWA or the state viewer for a deactivation date and reason.
- Search SDWA for an active system with a similar name at the same park, which may be a
  replacement PWS number.
- Update the WSD: either mark the source inactive or correct its `pws_number`.

```{r clarify-inactive}
sdwa_inactive |>
  arrange(desc(wsd_source_id %in% rapid_source_ids), park_unit) |>
  transmute(Park = park_unit,
            System = water_system_name,
            `PWS number` = pws_number_clean,
            `SDWA system` = pws_name,
            `SDWA status` = pws_activity_status,
            Population = population_served,
            `On rapid list` = wsd_source_id %in% rapid_source_ids) |>
  show_table(height = "350px")
```

## Appendix: alternatives considered

Other rules tested before choosing the current one. "Busy parks covered" counts busy
parks with at least one High source.

```{r alternatives}
# The earlier primary rule: at least 50% of the park's park-run population (all systems,
# including staff-only), with the same municipal check
old_share <- results_all |>
  filter(system_category %in% park_run_categories) |>
  distinct(park_unit, unit_id, population_estimate) |>
  group_by(park_unit) |>
  mutate(share_all = population_estimate / sum(population_estimate)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(park_unit, unit_id, share_all)

alt <- results |>
  left_join(old_share, by = c("park_unit", "unit_id")) |>
  mutate(high_scale = system_category == "High",
         busy = park_visitation_class == "High",
         pws = system_category %in% pws_categories,
         passes_municipal = n_municipal < n_park_run,
         earlier_rule = high_scale | (pws & coalesce(share_all, 0) >= 0.5 & busy & passes_municipal))

alternatives <- list(
  "High scale only" = alt$high_scale,
  "Earlier rule: 50%+ of park-run population at busy parks" = alt$earlier_rule,
  "Earlier rule plus all Moderate at busy parks" = alt$earlier_rule | (alt$system_category == "Moderate" & alt$busy),
  "Current rule (primary PWS at busy parks)" = alt$high_importance,
  "Current rule without the municipal check" = alt$high_scale | (alt$park_role == "Primary" & alt$pws & alt$busy),
  "Current rule plus secondary PWS" =
    alt$high_importance | (alt$park_role == "Secondary" & alt$pws & alt$busy & alt$passes_municipal)
)

imap_dfr(alternatives, function(selected, name) {
  selected <- coalesce(selected, FALSE)
  parks <- unique(alt$park_unit[selected])
  tibble(Rule = name,
         Sources = sum(selected),
         Parks = length(parks),
         `Busy parks covered` = paste0(sum(busy_parks %in% parks), " of ", length(busy_parks)))
}) |>
  show_table()
```
